text:
Ava: Quick QA — dashboard action row feels cramped on desktop and collapses awkwardly on 13\" laptops. Screenshot in thread. Thinking about tightening spacing tokens and maybe renaming `space-compact`? :thinking:

Jon: I can repro on my 13\" laptop. Primary ghost button outline looks too faint — at 2px the contrast drops below 3:1 in dark mode. Two quick fixes: use a slightly darker border color or increase the visible stroke (but hit area still needs to be 44px min).

Priya: Copy nit: the CTA currently says `Run`. I prefer `Launch` (matches other consoles). `Run job` reads weird in feature contexts. If we rename tokens, update copy references too.

Sam: Also seeing toasts overlap the FAB when there are 2+ toasts. On narrow widths they can end up under the table header. Suggest adding a dedicated stacking token (e.g. `z-toast`) and ensure toasts push content instead of overlapping when possible. Example CSS:``` .toast { z-index: var(--z-toast, 800); margin-bottom: 8px; } ```

DesignBot: a11y-scan: ghost-button-border-color fails AA small text on #121212 (contrast 2.7:1). Recommend border color at least WCAG 3:1 for icon-only affordances.

Ava: OK proposal to decide on: 1) rename `space-compact` -> `space-tight` to clarify intent, 2) enforce min hit target 44px for all buttons, 3) ghost border color -> `var(--surface-contrast-10)` (or pick value meeting 3:1), 4) introduce `--z-toast` and ensure toasts stack above table headers. Who can take PRs? :thumbsup:

Jon: I can take the tokens + hit-target PR. Will add token deprecation note and a migration guide snippet. I'll include screenshots and a simple visual regression test.

Priya: I'll update copy (strings + i18n keys) and drop notes in the spec about CTA naming.

Sam: I'll handle toast stacking + add an e2e regression that simulates multiple toasts on narrow view.

Ava: Sweet — assigning to Jon / Priya / Sam. I'll drop a tiny spec in Figma and link it here: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/dashboard-action-row-spacing. If anyone has objections to the `space-tight` name, say now. Otherwise I'll open the design ticket.

Jon: No objections. One thought: consider `space-condensed` vs `space-tight` for existing consumers. `condensed` is a bit more descriptive for layout density. Happy to include a short note in the PR about the naming rationale.

Priya: `condensed` works for me too, but consistency with other token names matters. I'll follow whichever the design ticket decides.

Ava: Good point. I'll add both options to the Figma spec and vote in the ticket. Thanks everyone! (reaction :thumbsup:)
